added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(K=4\), let \(\mathcal X=\{x\}\), let \(\rho(x)=1\), and fix \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\) and \(m_*\in(0,1)\).  Put \(M_0=(1+m_*)/2\).  There exist the explicit legal law \(p\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), direction \(g\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal J}\), and radius \(r_0>0\) constructed by \(\text{lem:finite-legal-probe}\) and \(\text{lem:k4-oriented-parity-certificate}\), with \(M(p)=M_0\), for which the following frontier holds.

First, \(E_{p,r}(g)=0\) for every \(0<r\le r_0\).  For every \(\kappa>0\) and all sufficiently small such \(r\), no choice of an integer \(N\ge1\) and rows \(a_1,\ldots,a_N\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal J}\) makes the even finite max-absolute-linear functional
\[
 V_{p,r}(z)=\max_{1\le\nu\le N}|a_\nu^{\mathsf T}z|
\]
can satisfy simultaneously
\[
 V_{p,r}(z)\le E_{p,r}(z)\quad\text{for every }z\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal J}
\tag{P1}
\]
and
\[
 \|\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(q)-\Phi(p)\|_\infty
 \le V_{p,r}(q-p)
\tag{P2}
\]
for every \(q\in\Delta(\mathcal J)\) satisfying \(\operatorname{supp}(q)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(p)\), \(\|q-p\|_\infty<\kappa r\), and \(M(q)>0\).

Second, on the same one-sided legal face, define the non-even functional on \(\operatorname{span}\{g\}\) by
\[
 W^{\mathrm{ray}}_{p,r}(tg)=\frac{(-t)_+}{M_0},\qquad t\in\mathbb R,
\]
satisfies
\[
 W^{\mathrm{ray}}_{p,r}(tg)\le E_{p,r}(tg),\qquad
 W^{\mathrm{ray}}_{p,r}(g)=0,
 \qquad
 W^{\mathrm{ray}}_{p,r}(-g)=M_0^{-1}>0.
\tag{P3}
\]
For every sufficiently small \(\tau\in(0,r)\), the opposite finite displacement \(q_\tau=p-\tau g\) admits an explicit nearby legal base \(b_\tau\in\mathcal B(p,r)\) such that
\[
 \|\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(q_\tau)-\Phi(p)\|_\infty
 =\frac{\tau}{M_0-2\tau}
 \le \|d_{b_\tau}(-\tau g)\|_\infty
 =\frac{\tau M_0}{(M_0-2\tau)^2}.
\tag{P4}
\]
Thus orientation is necessary for this finite-probe strategy and repairs parity and nearby-legal derivative domination on this face.  These conclusions do not establish a global simultaneous-face comparison or uniform coverage over all triangular arrays.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Choose the common explicit singleton-cell law \(p\) and direction \(g\) used in \(\text{lem:finite-legal-probe}\) and \(\text{lem:k4-oriented-parity-certificate}\).  Both constructions use \(M_0=(1+m_*)/2\), the same survivor margins, the same product coupling of those margins, and the same observed direction.  Replace their two positive radii by their minimum and call it \(r_0\).

By \(\text{lem:finite-legal-probe}\), for every \(0<r\le r_0\),
\[
 E_{p,r}(g)=0.
\tag{1}
\]
That lemma further states that for every \(\kappa>0\) and every sufficiently small such \(r\), the pointwise bound in \((\mathrm{P1})\) is incompatible with domination of all endpoint increments in \((\mathrm{P2})\) by any functional of the displayed even finite max-absolute-linear form.  This proves the first assertion.

By \(\text{lem:k4-oriented-parity-certificate}\), the non-even ray functional defined in the proposition obeys, for every \(t\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 W^{\mathrm{ray}}_{p,r}(tg)=\frac{(-t)_+}{M_0}
 \le E_{p,r}(tg).
\tag{2}
\]
Putting \(t=1\) and \(t=-1\) in \((2)\) gives all three relations in \((\mathrm{P3})\).  The same lemma constructs, for every sufficiently small \(\tau\in(0,r)\), a legal \(b_\tau\in\mathcal B(p,r)\) and proves exactly
\[
 \|\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(p-\tau g)-\Phi(p)\|_\infty
 =\frac{\tau}{M_0-2\tau}
 \le\|d_{b_\tau}(-\tau g)\|_\infty
 =\frac{\tau M_0}{(M_0-2\tau)^2},
\tag{3}
\]
which is \((\mathrm{P4})\).  Equations \((1)\)--\((3)\) prove the stated method frontier.  Neither cited lemma asserts a construction across simultaneous legal faces or a conditional critical-value transfer over arbitrary triangular arrays, so the final scope limitation follows without adding any further claim.
added_lemmas.justification: This proposition preserves the exact same-face method frontier proved by the two explicit legal witness lemmas: even probes are impossible, while orientation repairs only that face.
added_lemmas.gap: It does not supply a global construction over simultaneous legal faces or a critical-value transfer over arbitrary triangular arrays.
added_lemmas.consumer: This is a standalone delivered proposition and the direct consumer of both witness lemmas; it records the strongest proved conclusion without implying all-array uniform coverage.

open_obligations.what_is_open: This is the sole all-array inferential target: prove the displayed uniform legal-inner-neighborhood comparison and conditional lower-quantile bound over arbitrary triangular arrays, including arrays for which the common envelope scale and its \(1-\alpha\) quantile converge to zero.
open_obligations.obstruction: The explicit legal \(K=4\) singleton-cell proof refutes every even symmetric max-linear probe of the form \(\max_\nu|a_\nu^{\mathsf T}z|\).  The bounded oriented construction repairs parity and finite curvature only on that singleton face.  Global pointwise domination across simultaneous capacity, selection-total, and active-cut faces; complete legal latent-mass transfer with row-by-row covariance traction; relative lower-quantile transfer for the resulting non-even Gaussian maximum; and the exact-zero-scale local-flatness branch all remain unproved.
open_obligations.attempted: The symmetric route sought an even finite maximum of linear rows dominated by the legal envelope and capable of controlling ambient endpoint increments; the explicit \(K=4\) singleton-cell certificate disproves that route.  The distinct oriented route retained signed one-sided rows and successfully constructed a legal survivor-to-never-selected transfer on the singleton face, yielding the required parity and finite-curvature inequalities there.  Extending those oriented rows through simultaneous faces did not establish pointwise domination by the full legal envelope, a complete latent-transfer and covariance-traction certificate, relative non-even lower-quantile validity, or the exact-zero-scale branch.
open_obligations.partial_result: The following results remain proved: the legal observed-law image, nearby-base envelope, conditional critical value, and total rectangle are measurable; uniformly over \(P_n\in\mathcal M\), the fallback probability vanishes and the finite coordinate widths are \(O_{P_n}(n^{-1/2})\); every fixed separated regular face has exact oracle Gaussian \(1-\alpha\) calibration; the explicit \(K=4\) emerging-support, rare-atom, tied-cut diagnostic has the stated Gaussian limit and exact limiting coverage; the singleton-cell construction refutes every even symmetric-probe reduction; and \(\text{prop:oriented-probe-frontier}\) records that the oriented ray repairs parity and finite curvature on that singleton face.  None of these partial results establishes the displayed all-array comparison.

prose_updates.related_work: The accepted CausalSmith survivor-complier benefit result supplies the exact sharp endpoint formula and full-law sharpness; identification is imported rather than reproved. Angrist, Imbens, and Rubin (1996) support conditional instrument randomization, treatment consistency, and no defiers, while Dong and Heiler (2026) support treatment-mediated selection and outcome consistency together with covariate-specific weak selection monotonicity. The fixed \(\epsilon\) overlap bound and fixed \(m_*\) aggregate denominator floor are uniform-class strengthenings here. Fang and Santos (2019) and Hong and Li (2018) motivate derivative-aware resampling, but their generic results do not construct the required nearby legal observed laws. Frandsen and Pond (2025), Imai and Okamoto (2026), and Andrews and Guggenberger (2009) begin from regular, asymptotically linear, or standardized representations that do not resolve the present one-sided legal-face problem at vanishing scale. The standalone proposition \(\text{prop:oriented-probe-frontier}\) records the exact method frontier on one explicit \(K=4\) singleton-covariate face: every even finite max-absolute-linear probe satisfying legal-envelope domination fails to dominate all nearby endpoint increments, whereas the oriented ray repairs parity and supplies nearby-legal derivative domination of the opposite finite increment on that face. All-array legal comparison and critical-value transfer remain unresolved. Consequently, the proved measurability, width, separated-face calibration, diagnostic, negative symmetric certificate, and singleton-face oriented certificate do not establish all-array uniform joint coverage.
